title: usew-world-heavyweight
label: the 600 Pound Gorilla

won.source: Billed as the reigning World Heavyweight Champion on the federation's own Last Stand Control Center of 14 May 1995, which records that he took the belt from Rick O'Malley at the Holiday Rush.

note: Rick O'Malley is named in the same document as a former World Champion — the reign this one ended. The chain forward from here does not survive: El Maestro is billed on the 8 April 1996 Blow-Out as a former World Heavyweight Champion, and no document holds the changes between May 1995 and March 1996.

title: usew-world-heavyweight

won.source: Billed as the reigning USeW World Heavyweight Champion on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996; his own reign is described there as already established.

how: Pinned by “Mr. Machismo” Hank Thompson at Leprecharnage, after Freddy Flame slid a chair into the ring and Thompson powerbombed him onto it.
note: Won on a card this collection does not hold; no start date survives.

title: usew-world-heavyweight
label: “Mr. Machismo” Hank Thompson

won.source: Leprecharnage, served under this wing: “the winner of this contest . . . by pinfall and New USeW Heavyweight Champion . . . 'Mr. Machismo' HANK THOMPSON.”

how: Pinned by 187 at 17:07 on the Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996, hiptossed out of his own abdominal stretch into a cover.

title: usew-world-heavyweight

won.source: The Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996, served under this wing: “Your winner and NEW 2 time USeW World Heavyweight Champion........187!”

note: Still champion on 22 April 1996, the last card of this federation's own that this collection holds.

title: usew-world-television
label: Justice D. Nyde

won.source: Billed as the current USeW World Television Champion on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996.

how: Pinned by Jack Diamond at 34:44 at Leprecharnage, with the Diamond Senton.
note: The federation's own account of the four-way match that created this championship names both Haplo and Nyde as its champion in one sentence and then says Haplo retained; that contradiction is recorded on the title's own row and no earlier reign is written from it.

title: usew-world-television
label: Jack Diamond

won.source: Leprecharnage: “The winner of this contest . . . and NEW USeW WORLD TELEVISION CHAMPION . . . JACK DIAMOND.”

how: Pinned by El Maestro at 3:18 on the Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996, with a Northern lights suplex.

title: usew-world-television
label: El Maestro

won.source: The Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996: “We have a new Television champion!”

how: Pinned by Simon Sanders at 5:21 on the Monday Night Blow-Out of 22 April 1996, with the Boogie-Woogie Jam-Slam.

won.source: The Monday Night Blow-Out of 22 April 1996: “the winner of this contest . . . and NEW USeW TELEVISION CHAMPION . . . SILKY SMOOTH SIMON SANDERS.”

title: usew-world-television-tag-team
label: BlackJack

won.source: Billed as the USeW World Television Tag Team Champions on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996, and described there as having held the belts “for a little while now” with several defences already made.

how: Lost the titles to Doom and Disaster at 29:15 on the Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996.
note: Kept the belts at Leprecharnage by losing the match: their own manager hit a challenger with a title belt in front of the referee and the team was disqualified.

title: usew-world-television-tag-team
label: Doom and Disaster

won.source: The Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996: “Winners: Doom and Disaster +6 (Blackjack -3).”

note: Kept the titles on 22 April 1996 the same way the previous champions had: disqualified against La Famiglia at 7:43 after using a belt, and still champions.

title: usew-world-tag-team
label: the Machismos

won.source: Billed as the current World Tag Team Champions on the federation's own Last Stand Control Center of 14 May 1995, with a title defence against the number one contenders already signed.

note: The Iconoclasts are named in the same document as former World Tag Champions — an earlier reign this collection cannot date.

title: usew-world-tag-team
label: the White Knights

won.source: Billed as the reigning and undefeated USeW World Tag Team Champions on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996.

note: Retained against the Equalizers at Leprecharnage in 3:36, the shortest World Tag Team title match in this federation's own held record.

title: usew-light-heavyweight
label: Swashbuckler Jack Hornblower

won.source: Billed as the USeW Light-Heavyweight Champion on the federation's own Last Stand Control Center of 14 May 1995, having kept the belt at the Holiday Rush after a branding-iron attack.

note: Booked to defend it in a Texas Death Match against the man who attacked him; the card is not held.

title: usew-light-heavyweight
label: Doug Carr

won.source: Billed as the current USeW Light Heavyweight Champion on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996.

note: Retained against “Suicidal” Sean Altman at Leprecharnage in 9:24. Simon Sanders is separately billed on the same card's own aftermath as a former Light Heavyweight Champion — a reign this collection cannot date.

title: usew-united-states-heavyweight
label: the Nightcreeper

won.source: Billed on the federation's own Last Stand Control Center of 14 May 1995 as “the newly-crowned United States Heavyweight Champion.”

note: The card that would have followed is not held, and no other document of this championship survives.

title: usew-north-american
label: Comanche War Dog

won.source: Billed on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996, as the former USeW North American Champion, stripped of the title three weeks earlier.

how: Stripped by the federation, which abolished the championship in the same announcement.

end.source: Leprecharnage's own recap: “Three weeks ago, Comanche War Dog was stripped of the North American Title for a few reasons.”
